one_line_contribution: A controlled measurement, in ALFWorld with deterministic prefix replay, of how much of a retrieved item's counterfactual value is a property of the moment it is consumed (entry / procedure-due / post-stuck recovery) rather than of the item or its class, using paired leave-one-out contrasts on manufactured item classes at a common prefix, plus a test of whether entry-trained per-item scores retain rank signal at recovery.
closest_prior_work: The Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608, verified via s2cli paper lookup and returned by my mechanism and recent queries) is the most direct threat: it is a trajectory-level diagnosis of how agents consume retrieved memory across a multi-step action trajectory, and its headline finding is exactly position-dependent memory harm — early adoption of conflicting memory compounds errors and produces weak recovery. That is the qualitative content of P2 (mismatched item harmful, harm located at a stage rather than in the item) already in print. It does not fully pre-empt the proposal, because its unit is the conflicting-memory condition at the first exposed decision point rather than a per-item paired counterfactual at three pre-registered stages of a replayed common prefix, and it does not decompose value into class vs stage vs interaction. Second threat, also verified: MERIT / 'Learning to Retrieve: Dual-Level Long-Term Memory for Text-to-SQL Agents' (arXiv:2606.00547, S2, cit 2), whose entire motivation is that memory usefulness differs across interaction stages, operationalized as episode- vs turn-level retrieval; the proposal's premise is that paper's design assumption, so the contribution reduces to measuring a premise others have already acted on. SLEA-RL (arXiv:2603.18079, verified) makes step-conditioned retrieval standard, and MemHarness (arXiv:2607.28272, verified) already attributes negative transfer to verbatim replay of context-mismatched experience and shows reconstruction removes it — which is the proposal's own A1 control, i.e. the mechanism-removal result is partly known.
strongest_objection: The headline estimand is not identifiable independently of choices the authors make. Two compounding problems. (1) P3 compares a class x stage interaction component against a class main-effect component over a class menu the authors manufacture, and the menu is deliberately stocked with a class (I2, location-mismatched) designed to be harmful specifically at recovery; adding or dropping such classes moves the interaction component arbitrarily, so 'interaction >= class identity' is a statement about the item menu, not about memory. No CI or MDE is stated anywhere for (interaction - class), the primary quantity. (2) The primary scale manufactures the effect: on the headroom-normalized scale, any class whose raw value is stage-stable — precisely what P1 predicts for I1+I4 — becomes interaction because the divisor differs per stage, so P1's confirmation mechanically supports P3. Layered on this is a selection problem the intersection-subset fix does not solve: S2 prefixes exist only where the k=0 run got stuck, and that same k=0 run is the S0 'without' arm, so the intersection subset over which the decomposition and the DiD are computed consists of games where the baseline reader failed, a population on which the pre-registered positive controls (I1 at S0 reproduces +21.5, I4 reproduces +12.4, both measured on the full 274-game set) provide no validation of the cells that carry the headline. Finally, the automated entailment check finds P1 and P5 unresolvable at the stated budget (the P1 confirm band <= +4 sits wholly inside a +/-5.7 CI with the falsifier at +6; P5's +8 threshold equals its own +/-8 half-width) and P2's DiD threshold of +12 sits at its +/-11 CI, so of five predictions only the I2-harm half of P2 is comfortably decidable — a fatal profile for a paper whose sole contribution is measurement.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes. (a) Make the raw-scale decomposition primary and require the interaction >= class claim on both scales, and pre-register a bootstrap MDE for (interaction - class) from the T0 pilot; a headline estimand with no stated power is not pre-registered. (b) Fix the identifiability of P3 by reporting the decomposition under a leave-one-class-out jackknife over the I1-I5 menu, so a reader sees how much of the interaction is carried by the class built to be stage-sensitive, and report per-class stage profiles as the primary object instead of a single menu-dependent ratio. (c) Add the carried-item arm (see missing_baseline) so the stage contrast is about consumption moment rather than insertion event. (d) Re-budget for decidability: drop T4' and one of the 1-seed ablations and spend the ~2,200 episode-equivalents on seeds for the S2 four-arm interaction until its half-width is <= 4, move P1 to a pre-registered TOST equivalence bound on the confirm side, and re-derive P2's DiD threshold at ~2 CI widths. Also state the S0 cell values restricted to the intersection subset alongside the full-set positive controls, so the reader can see whether the S0 anchor survives conditioning on baseline failure.
missing_baseline: The carried-from-entry arm: the same item injected at step 0 and still present in context at the S2 (or S1) prefix, evaluated against the same paired no-item continuation. Every stage arm as designed is a mid-episode insertion of new prompt text, so 'value at recovery' is confounded with 'novel text appearing mid-prompt after a stuck streak'; the cross-type placebo controls for appended text but not for text-appended-now vs text-present-all-along. This matters because deployed entry-retrieval systems (and the k=1/k=3 sweep the whole program is anchored to) keep the item in context through the stuck phase, so the proposal's S2 condition matches no deployed configuration and the P2 sign contrast may be an insertion effect rather than a stage effect. The mirror arm (item present in the replayed prefix, removed at S2) would be the cheap complement. A secondary omission: a stage-aware re-retrieval arm (item selected at S2 by a query built from the current observation, SLEA-RL-style) appears only as a scorer for the fixed item set, never as a competing intervention, so the paper cannot say whether stage-indexing the value table buys anything a stage-conditioned query does not already buy.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. Channel for all four of my queries: the s2cli literature command (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers, s2=ok hf=ok on every run); WebSearch is unavailable in this session and was not used. Q1 (mechanism, unrestricted) 'stage-conditional value of retrieved memory item injected at different points of an episode LLM agent' -> 12 hits, nearest 2608.15008 (regime-dependent memory substrates), 2603.02473 (retrieval vs utilization bottlenecks), 2603.04549 (A-MAC admission); none does per-item stage-conditional counterfactuals. Q2 (mechanism, --recent) 'when memory helps versus hurts depends on the stage of the episode retrieval timing counterfactual leave-one-out agent' -> 9 hits, top 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap), 2606.22844 (RaMem), 2605.12978 (useful memories become faulty when updated); the first is the real threat, the rest are off-claim. Q3 (closest named method) 'dual-level memory turn-level versus episode-level retrieval usefulness varies across interaction stages agent' -> 10 hits, returned 2607.10608, 2606.22844, 2605.18421, 2601.05107; notably MERIT itself did not surface by description, so I verified it by id. Q4 (per-item credit, --recent) 'per-item counterfactual credit leave-one-out value of individual retrieved experience item agent memory sign flip helps then hurts' -> 8 hits, relevant: 2604.05467 (CUE-R, per-item REMOVE/REPLACE utility but single-shot RAG, not multi-step, no stage axis), 2608.18852 (SkillGate, misleading skill exposure), 2603.21563 (counterfactual credit for multi-agent); no multi-step per-item stage-conditional counterfactual found. IDs verified by s2cli paper lookup: 2606.00547 (returned as 'Learning to Retrieve: Dual-Level Long-Term Memory for Text-to-SQL Agents', S2, 2026-05-30, cit 2 — the proposal's 'MERIT' label matches the method name in the abstract), 2607.28272 (MemHarness, 2026-07-30), 2603.18079 (SLEA-RL, 2026-03-18), 2606.29502 (UCOB, 2026-06-28, cit 9), 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap, 2026-07-12), 2601.05107 (Controllable Memory Usage, 2026-01-08); 2604.05467 verified indirectly by appearing in Q4. Not verified: the home-literature ids 2211.07882, 2404.08828, 2502.04576, 2608.01953, 2605.12004, the 'seen under another query' id 2608.30177, and U-EHR, which is cited as 'KDD 2026' with no arXiv id and is therefore unverifiable as written — the proposal should give it an id. Judgement on the proposal's own check: it is above average for this program — it names the channel, gives ids, reports one query as returning nothing, and separates home-literature from mechanism queries — but it has one substantive hole. It cites 2606.00547 in Related Work as the paper that 'argues memory usefulness changes across interaction stages', i.e. the proposal's own premise, and then never runs a collision query against that premise; the check's recency queries are aimed at negative transfer and step-level retrieval instead. An honest check would have asked whether MERIT's or the Compliance Trap's motivating measurements already establish the stage-dependence the proposal treats as its finding, and would have conceded that what remains new is the estimator (paired counterfactual at a replayed common prefix) rather than the phenomenon.
